title: POC hosting strategy engagement brief
body:
Purpose:
This brief captures an engagement-level recommendation for the upcoming retail POC (purchase intent and store-assistant flows). The customer is evaluating three modes: hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated Reserved Capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). Goal is a small, timeboxed POC to validate latency-sensitive features and data controls with a path to production.

Context and constraints (from kickoff):
- Traffic: expected 50-200 concurrent interactive users during store-hours for the POC, peak request rate ~30 req/s with median prompt size ~400 tokens.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 300ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens) for the live demo experience; background batch/analytics can be relaxed.
- Data controls: customer requires that user chat logs for PII flows be segregated; audit trail required.
- Timeline: 6-week POC, demo at week 6.
- Budget: POC budget constrained; willingness to pay for dedicated if it reduces integration risk.

High-level recommendation (short):
Run a hybrid POC: start hosted (fast onboarding) for feature validation and UX iteration, then run a 2-week dedicated-capacity window mid-POC to validate throughput, SLOs, and cost profiles. Reserve Private (VPC) evaluation only if dedicated fails security audit or latency cannot be met in-region.

Rationale (why hybrid):
- Hosted gets us live quickly: minimal infra setup, simple SDK and streaming, which lets product and SRE validate UX and edge cases in weeks 0–2.
- Dedicated lets us measure predictable latency and per-token cost under committed capacity; helps quantify economics for the customer's peak patterns.
- Private is high-confidence for security but adds setup time and operational overhead; for a short POC it’s high friction unless required by contract.

Deployment options considered and tradeoffs:
1) Hosted-only
  - Pros: fastest onboarding, lowest project ops, immediate model catalog access, automatic region routing.
  - Cons: noisy neighbors at very high peaks; limited ability to pin hardware/quantization; may not pass strict enterprise audit.
  - When to pick: if legal team accepts data residency and SLOs can be demonstrated in-region.

2) Dedicated (reserved pool burst-enabled)
  - Pros: predictable latency, capacity isolation, cost predictability under commit, supports canary rollouts and model pinning.
  - Cons: longer lead time to provision reserved GPUs, needs autoscaling policy tuning, some dev work to integrate tracing and rollout hooks.
  - When to pick: if the customer wants a predictable unit cost and an SLA they can rely on for demo and go-live.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem)
  - Pros: customer controls networking, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs under their tenancy, can meet strict compliance needs.
  - Cons: longest setup time, cross-team coordination, potential hardware procurement or network peering work, ops responsibilities shift to customer or SEP (professional services).
  - When to pick: mandatory for regulated data or if the customer requires air-gapped environment.

Workload fingerprinting (how we decide at run time):
- Step 1: Instrument initial hosted run with telemetry collection (token counts, seq length distribution, cold vs warm cache ratio, tail latencies per model).
- Step 2: After 7–10 days, compute the workload fingerprint (median seq length, top-5 prompt shapes, KV cache hit rate).
- Step 3: Use fingerprint to simulate Dedicated sizing (GPU type, batch size, expected throughput) and estimate per-token cost difference.
- Decision: if predicted dedicated cost <20% above hosted and latency improvement >35% at 95th, recommend Dedicated trial.

Latency/Cost estimation (ballpark for planning):
- Hosted: expected median latency 80–160ms (short prompts), 95th ~280–400ms depending on region; per-token cost baseline = $X* (customer billing TBD).
- Dedicated (A100-equivalent pool): median latency 30–90ms, 95th < 200ms under correct batching; per-token cost may drop 15–40% vs hosted at sufficient commit.
- Private: latency similar to Dedicated when colocated; incremental dev/ops costs significant.

Security and compliance checklist for POC:
- Data classification mapping: identify which prompts/responses contain PII, mark for encryption-at-rest and restricted access.
- Retention policy: set demo retention to 7 days unless customer requests otherwise.
- Audit logs: enable request-level logging and supply a daily extract to customer (hosted) or configure Splunk/ELK (dedicated/private).
- KMS: for Private, integrate with customer KMS; for Hosted evaluate envelope encryption and key access policy.
- Pen test: schedule an expedited security review in week 3 if moving to Dedicated/Private.

Operational plan (6-week timeline):
- Week 0 (kickoff, infra prep): agree success criteria, allocate hosted test keys, instrument telemetry. Owner: Ava.
- Week 1–2 (rapid UX iteration on hosted): product flows, streaming checks, error handling, plug in analytics. Owner: Solutions Eng / Product.
- Week 3 (fingerprint + decision gate): analyze telemetry, compute Dedicated sizing, security review check. Owner: Ravi (telemetry), Sofia (security).
- Week 4–5 (dedicated trial window, optional): provision reserved pool, run traffic replay for 2 weeks, collect cost/latency metrics. Owner: Marcus (infra), SRE support.
- Week 6 (demo + retrospective): present findings, recommended path to production, follow-ups for enterprise procurement if needed. Owner: Ava.

Success criteria (pass/fail for POC):
- Functional: core retail assistant flows complete end-to-end with streaming and function-calling where applicable.
- Latency: 95th percentile < 300ms for short prompts in demo region (measured during normal demo load).
- Security: basic audit logs and retention policy implemented; customer sign-off on data classification.
- Economics: per-token cost estimate and Dedicated sizing documented for go/no-go.

Open questions / customer risks:
- Will procurement approve a short Dedicated reservation for the trial? (alternatively we can use burstable Dedicated or a short-term cloud spot pool to approximate).
- Does the customer's privacy team require Private by default for PII (would add ~3–6 weeks to setup)?
- Are there regulatory constraints for data residency in specific EU region(s)?

Fallbacks and mitigation plan:
- If hosted 95th tail is too high in region: schedule Dedicated window ASAP and implement region routing to closest Redwood POP.
- If Dedicated provisioning delays: use workload replay from hosted instrumentation and run autoscaling stress tests on a small on-demand pool to approximate behavior.
- If Private required late in POC: scope a minimal private sandbox (single-node VPC deployment) to meet audit needs for demo and plan full roll after contract.

Deliverables for customer at close of POC:
- POC report (this includes telemetry dump, fingerprint, Dedicated sizing, cost model)
- Demo recording and runbook for production cutover
- Security assessment summary and recommended controls
- Roadmap for production modes with estimated timelines and costs

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Share brief with customer and schedule the fingerprint call (Owner: Ava)
- Create JIRA-POC-1293 tasks for telemetry instrumentation and demo data set (Owner: Ravi)
- Confirm Dedicated reservation windows and pricing with sales (Owner: Marcus)

Notes to self / lower priority items:
- Consider running a microbench with quantized variants to see whether cheaper model variants can meet UX bar (may influence Dedicated sizing).
- Track prefix-cache hit rates; caching could materially change cost calculus for repeat queries.

End of brief.

Appendix: quick decision matrix (text)
- Priority: Latency | Data control | Speed-to-demo
- Hosted: Medium | Low-Medium | High
- Dedicated: High | Medium | Medium
- Private: High | High | Low

If you want, I can convert this into a slide deck for the customer demo or a short one-page comparison for procurement.
